malinois.intro: A security-review lens that stays on all session, plus on-demand audits.
malinois.lens: The always-on lens flags injection, broken authz/authn, secrets, SSRF, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, weak crypto and insecure defaults as you work.

commands.does: Static audit of a source repo (SAST + dependency CVEs + secrets)
Assessment of a running web app (scope-gated)
Merge the session's findings into one ranked report

checks.d: SQL/NoSQL/OS command/LDAP/template. String-built queries or shell from untrusted input. Fix: parameterize, use the platform's safe API.
missing ownership/role check per object (IDOR/BOLA), client-trusted role, endpoints with no guard.
weak token checks (`<` vs `<=` on expiry), predictable ids, missing signature verification, fixation.
hardcoded keys, tokens, passwords in source, config, history. Redact in any output; never echo full secret.
user-controlled URLs or paths reaching fetch/file APIs.
pickle, native deserialize, `eval`, template eval on untrusted data.
MD5/SHA1 for passwords, ECB, static IV, homemade crypto, no constant-time compare.
debug on, permissive CORS/CSP, verbose errors, TLS verify off.

rules: Authorized, in-scope targets only. Static review of code the user owns is fine. Active testing (requests/scans/fuzzing against a live system) needs the target in the user's written scope — if unclear, ask and wait.
Findings first. Write PoC/exploit code only when the user asks AND the target is in scope.
Root cause over symptom: grep every caller before you call something safe.
End each review with: what you did not check, and the top risk the user must act on.

husky.intro: A misconfiguration lens for infrastructure-as-code that stays on all session, plus an on-demand audit.
husky.lens: The always-on lens flags public exposure, wildcard IAM, secrets in config, privileged containers, missing encryption/logging and CI supply-chain risks as you work.

commands.does: Static audit of Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, Dockerfiles and CI pipelines

checks.d: buckets/blobs public, security groups `0.0.0.0/0` on admin ports (22, 3389, DB ports), public DB instances, LoadBalancer services with no auth.
`Action: "*"` / `Resource: "*"`, `iam:PassRole` broad, assumable roles with `Principal: "*"`, long-lived access keys, cluster-admin bindings for workloads.

credentials in tfvars, manifests, Dockerfile `ENV`/`ARG`, CI env, state files committed. Never print a secret's value — not keys, tokens, passwords (even weak or default ones), or connection strings. Name the file:line and the kind of secret only, e.g. `password default (redacted)`. Writing a value and labelling it redacted is a leak.
`privileged: true`, `hostNetwork`/`hostPID`, `hostPath` mounts, running as root, no resource limits, `allowPrivilegeEscalation`, `:latest` images.
storage/DB/volumes unencrypted, TLS off, audit/flow logs disabled, no versioning on state buckets.
`pull_request_target` checking out PR code, unpinned third-party actions, `permissions: write-all`, secrets exposed to forks, `curl | sh`.

rules: Static review only. Never run `terraform apply`, `kubectl apply`, or any state-changing cloud call.
Root cause over symptom: follow modules, variables and defaults before calling something safe.
End each review with: what you did not check, and the top risk the user must act on.

collie.intro: A security lens for LLM apps and agents that stays on all session, plus an on-demand audit.
collie.lens: The always-on lens treats the model as untrusted and flags prompt injection (direct and indirect), over-powered tools, model output reaching shell/SQL/`eval`/HTML, cross-tenant retrieval, secrets and PII in prompts or logs, risky MCP config, and unbounded agent loops.

commands.does: Static audit of an LLM app or agent: prompts, tools, RAG, MCP config and model-output handling

checks.d: user input concatenated into system prompts; tools that fetch web pages, emails, files or tickets and feed them back unfenced (indirect injection).
tools that run shell, write files, send messages, spend money or call internal APIs with no allowlist, no human confirmation and broad credentials.
model output reaching `eval`/`exec`, shell, SQL strings, file paths, or rendered as raw HTML/Markdown (XSS, image-URL exfiltration).
secrets or keys in prompts; RAG retrieval without tenant/ACL filters; PII in prompts, logs or traces; system prompt treated as a secret.
servers with filesystem root `/`, auto-approve on everything, unpinned `@latest` packages, tokens in config.
no max iterations, max tokens, timeouts or rate limits on agent loops.

rules: Static review only. Never fire payloads at a live model or endpoint.
Never print a secret's value — not keys, tokens or passwords, even weak defaults. Give file:line and the secret type only.
End each review with: what you did not check, and the top risk the user must act on.
collie.bench: `bench/` holds a Python support agent (Anthropic SDK, Flask, RAG, MCP config) with 18 planted issues, 2 decoys and an answer key.

bloodhound.intro: A security lens for REST and GraphQL APIs that stays on all session, plus an on-demand audit. It reads the spec and the handlers together, because most API bugs live in the gap between them.
bloodhound.lens: The always-on lens follows the OWASP API Top 10: object- and function-level authorization, broken authentication, mass assignment and over-shared fields, missing rate/size/depth limits, unbounded business flows, SSRF, misconfiguration, and shadow or zombie endpoints.

commands.does: Static audit of a REST or GraphQL API: inventories spec vs. routes, then checks every operation

checks.d: handler loads a resource by id from the path/body without checking it belongs to the caller.
tokens decoded but not verified, no expiry, API keys in query strings, operations marked `security: []`.
mass assignment (`additionalProperties: true`, spreading request bodies into models); responses returning fields the caller must not see.
no rate limit, no max page size, unbounded GraphQL depth/complexity, no request size cap.
admin or internal operations reachable by ordinary users.
money/quantity fields without bounds, missing idempotency, replayable actions.
user-supplied URLs (webhooks, imports, avatars) fetched by the server.
permissive CORS with credentials, verbose errors, `http://` servers, GraphQL introspection in production.
routes in code but not in the spec (shadow), old versions still mounted (zombie).

rules: Static review only. Never hit a live API unless it is in the user's written scope.
Never print a secret's value — not keys, tokens or passwords, even weak defaults. Give file:line and the secret type only.
End each review with: what you did not check, and the top risk the user must act on.
bloodhound.bench: `bench/` holds an Express + Apollo GraphQL ledger API with an OpenAPI spec: 18 planted issues, 2 decoys, an answer key, and no hint comments. Several criticals only show up by reading the router mount order in `app.js` against the spec.

request/response bodies, user objects or tokens logged; error trackers capturing PII.
analytics, ads and crash SDKs receiving PII or device ids; data sent cross-border.
tracking that fires before consent; no way to withdraw.
no TTL or purge; account deletion that leaves copies in backups, caches, search indexes.
APIs and exports returning more personal data than the screen needs; PII in URLs.
no path to export or delete a user's data (GDPR Art. 15/17, DPDP s.11-13).

rules: Static review only. Never change live systems or send traffic to targets outside the user's written scope.
Never print a secret's value — not keys, tokens or passwords, even weak defaults. Give file:line and the secret type only.

guessable or non-expiring tokens, token in response, no invalidation after use.
bypassable step, recovery codes in plaintext, MFA not enforced on sensitive actions.
email-based auto-linking, unverified emails trusted.
